title: Trump Was Still Scolding Allies for Not Saluting His Hormuz Gamble
description_short: Trump Was Still Scolding Allies for Not Saluting His Hormuz Gamble
description_medium: Trump said he was unhappy with Australia for not joining U.S. activity around the Strait of Hormuz, but did not identify a specific request. Australia’s Defense Minister Richard Marles said no specific request had been made, and Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said there had been no new requests. Australia had deployed a surveillance aircraft to help defend Gulf allies.
description_long: Donald Trump again criticized Australia over its role in the conflict around the Strait of Hormuz, telling reporters he was “not happy with Australia because they were not there when we asked them to be there.” When asked what the United States had requested, he did not give a direct answer and referred to the strait. Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said there had been no new requests. Deputy Prime Minister and Defense Minister Richard Marles said Australia had received no specific request concerning Hormuz, although it had received a general call to help defend Gulf allies and deployed a Wedgetail surveillance aircraft. Marles said Australia would work with partners on reopening the shipping channel when circumstances allowed. The Guardian reported that leaders were due to discuss the strait at a Paris summit. The exchange came amid the wider Iran war and disagreement over allied support. It documents Trump’s public complaint and the Australian government’s account of the requests; it does not establish that Australia refused a specific U.S. operation or that the two governments ended their cooperation.

preserved_fields.title: Trump Was Still Scolding Allies for Not Saluting His Hormuz Gamble
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump Was Still Scolding Allies for Not Saluting His Hormuz Gamble

notes: Replaced the prior editorial characterization with Trump’s comments and the Australian officials’ response. The linked report says Australia had deployed surveillance support for Gulf allies, while Marles denied a specific Hormuz request.

title: Trump's Presidential Library Looked Like a Self-Worship Casino in Waiting
description_short: Trump's Presidential Library Looked Like a Self-Worship Casino in Waiting
description_medium: The Guardian reviewed renderings for a proposed 47-story Trump presidential library on Miami’s waterfront, including a large gold statue and hotel-like features. The article was an architecture critique, not a report that a library or hotel had been built. Trump himself told reporters the project would most likely be a hotel; the site and design remained proposals in the report.
description_long: The Guardian’s April 3, 2026, architecture feature examined renderings for a proposed 47-story Trump presidential library on Miami’s waterfront. The design included a large gold statue of Trump and a mirrored tower; the article’s critic described the scheme as self-glorifying and compared its presentation to a luxury hotel. Trump told reporters, “I don’t believe in building libraries or museums,” and said the project would most likely be a hotel. His son Eric Trump, co-chair of the nonprofit foundation seeking donations for the project, presented the design as a lasting tribute. The proposal came after Miami-Dade College transferred waterfront land to the foundation. A judge dismissed a challenge to the transfer that argued the college’s board had not provided sufficient notice for public discussion. The report also noted that the site was valued at more than $67 million. These details concern a proposed project and an architectural critic’s interpretation, not a completed building or established misuse of public money. The article did not document construction or the final program for the site.

preserved_fields.title: Trump's Presidential Library Looked Like a Self-Worship Casino in Waiting
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump's Presidential Library Looked Like a Self-Worship Casino in Waiting

notes: Distinguishes the proposed project and opinionated architecture review from completed construction or a finding of financial misconduct.

title: Trump's Party Got a Fresh Texas Gerrymander Back From the Supreme Court
description_short: Trump's Party Got a Fresh Texas Gerrymander Back From the Supreme Court
description_medium: The Supreme Court formally reinstated Texas’s congressional map, which the Republican-led legislature approved in 2025 and Gov. Greg Abbott signed. The map was designed to improve Republican prospects and could shift as many as five seats. The ruling reversed a lower court that had found the map likely racially discriminatory; it did not decide the 2026 election outcome.
description_long: On April 27, 2026, the Supreme Court formally reinstated Texas’s congressional map, finalizing an interim decision from December that allowed the state to use it. The Republican-led Texas legislature approved the map in August 2025 and Gov. Greg Abbott signed it. The map was drawn to increase Republican representation and could shift as many as five seats currently held by Democrats, according to the Guardian. The Court reversed a lower-court ruling that had blocked the map after finding it likely violated constitutional protections against racial discrimination. The three liberal justices dissented from the Supreme Court’s decision. Trump had urged Republican lawmakers to redraw congressional districts to improve his party’s prospects in the 2026 midterms; Republicans held narrow majorities in both chambers of Congress at the time. The decision permitted Texas to use the map, but the projected seat changes were possibilities, not election results. The report described a broader wave of mid-decade redistricting by both parties, including a separate California map the Court allowed in February. It did not establish how voters would respond or how many seats either party would win.

preserved_fields.title: Trump's Party Got a Fresh Texas Gerrymander Back From the Supreme Court
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump's Party Got a Fresh Texas Gerrymander Back From the Supreme Court

notes: Reports the Supreme Court’s action and lower-court finding with attribution; the map’s projected partisan effects are not treated as election results.

title: Donald Trump enrolls at Fordham University
description_short: Donald Trump enrolls at Fordham University
description_medium: Fordham’s student newspaper reports that Trump attended the university’s Bronx campus for two years before transferring to the University of Pennsylvania, where he completed his degree in 1968. A 1965 Fordham yearbook lists him as a freshman and member of the squash team. The exact enrollment day is not established by the linked account; the timeline’s July 1 date is unsupported.
description_long: Donald Trump studied at Fordham University’s Rose Hill campus in the Bronx before transferring to the University of Pennsylvania. In interviews with alumni, Fordham’s student newspaper reported that he commuted from Queens and attended Fordham for two years. The article says he later completed his degree at Penn in 1968 and notes that Fordham’s 1965 yearbook lists him as a freshman on the squash team. That yearbook provides a contemporaneous reference for his enrollment by 1965, while the alumni interviews add recollections of his daily commute and student life. The supplied timeline labels the event July 1, 1964, but the cited account does not establish that exact date; the entry should not present it as confirmed. The source does not support the separate allegation in the synopsis that Trump’s sister completed homework for him, so that claim is omitted. These materials support a short educational chronology, but a personal enrollment entry does not fit the project’s available categories for political or institutional harms.

preserved_fields.title: Donald Trump enrolls at Fordham University
preserved_fields.description_short: Donald Trump enrolls at Fordham University

notes: The Fordham account supports two years of attendance, transfer to Penn, and a 1965 yearbook entry, but not the timeline’s exact July 1 date or the sister-homework allegation. No supplied canonical category fits this personal education record.
proposed_correction: Change the date to the supported year or provide a source for July 1, 1964; remove the homework allegation unless independently supported. Omit this personal education record from the harm-focused categories or add an appropriate biographical category.

title: Donald Trump is investigated for bribery, possible mob ties
description_short: Donald Trump is investigated for bribery, possible mob ties
description_medium: In his 1992 biography of Donald Trump, journalist Wayne Barrett wrote that Trump had been the subject of a bribery investigation in 1979. Barrett connected the allegation to New York’s construction industry. The supplied account says the inquiry ended without an indictment, but provides no investigative records or account from the agency involved.

preserved_fields.title: Donald Trump is investigated for bribery, possible mob ties
preserved_fields.description_short: Donald Trump is investigated for bribery, possible mob ties

notes: The available account attributes the claim to Barrett’s 1992 biography and does not include contemporary investigative records or a full description of the inquiry’s disposition. It remains an allegation, not a finding of guilt.
proposed_correction: Keep the claim attributed to Barrett and obtain contemporary investigative records or additional reliable reporting before presenting the investigation’s scope and outcome as established fact.
